transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 2026-02-20T15:00:00Z
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Sam Patel, Jordan Lee (Redwood); Maya Rodriguez, Derek Nguyen, Priya Singh (Velarix)

Summary (auto): QBR focused on usage, cost, reliability, roadmap alignment and security requirements.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. happy qbr, i'm avery from redwood, with sam and jordan. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: doing well, thanks. busy month for us, lots of adoption in the new support flow.
[00:18] Derek: yep sorry for the slight chaos, we're ramping to prod for two features.
[00:25] Sam: excellent. quick agenda: usage/cost trends, reliability/latency, security ask, and roadmap + next steps. sound good?
[00:34] Priya: perfect.
[00:36] Avery: cool, maya can you kick off with a quick recap of what's changed on your end?
[00:40] Maya: sure. over the last 8 weeks we've doubled inference volume for our customer support chatbot. month-to-date tokens are around 120M, up from 55M in december, so pretty big. most of that is short chat sessions but a non-trivial percent are long context threads, we hit 4k-6k token sequences some times.
[01:05] Avery: thanks, that matches what we see in the console. your cost is trending up, we've got a summarized chart we can send, but before that can you describe if the latency sensitivity changed?
[01:17] Maya: yes, the support flow is end-user facing so p95 latency matters — users start to notice above 300ms. we've seen spikes during 11am-1pm PT where p95 nudges toward 380-450ms. p99 is worse, sometimes 900-1.2s during big bursts.
[01:36] Sam: okay noted. do you have autoscaling configured on the hosted plan? and are you using any prefix caching / reuse patterns?
[01:45] Maya: autoscaling yes but it's default, burst has been ok but cost is creeping. we do reuse prompts a bit but not full prefix caching yet — that's on the roadmap.
[01:55] Derek: one of our asks is whether dedicated reserved capacity would lower unit cost and stabilize tail latency. we don't want to manage GPUs ourselves ideally.
[02:05] Sam: yeah, that's a classic tradeoff. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token cost if you commit. it also reduces noisy neighbor and warm start issues that cause p99 spikes. we can run a small benchmark to quantify.
[02:18] Priya: from infra side we also need VPC peering and KMS integration. we handle keys in-house and need envelope encryption for any persistent KV caches.
[02:28] Jordan: got it — we support KMS/HSM, and we can share our SOC 2 package. for Dedicated / Private setups we do provide private control plane options and audit logs.
[02:39] Maya: great, can you send the SOC 2 docs and a KMS integration guide after this?
[02:44] Avery: absolutely, we'll add that to next steps.
[02:47] [00:03:00] Sam: quick clarifying question: you mentioned 4k-6k token sequences — are those mostly single-turn or multi-turn threads?
[03:04] Maya: multi-turn, the agent history plus attachments summarized. sometimes we pass a 2k system prompt plus a 2-3k conversation.
[03:13] Sam: thanks, that'll influence KV cache effectiveness and checkpointing. longer sequences are where quantization and kernel selection matter for perf.
[03:24] Avery: on costs, our console shows your average spend this month around $7.8k to date, which annualizes higher if volume stays this way. dedicated reserved pool could bring that down depending on commit level. we'll share a few price bands.
[03:40] Derek: what's typical commit sizes customers pick for similar workloads?
[03:45] Sam: customers with this profile often start with a 2-4 node reserved pool and a small burst bucket. it depends on qps and seq length; we'll put together a recommendation after the bench.
[03:55] Maya: also curious about model choices — we saw some variance in quality between open models. can you recommend recs for low-latency vs high-quality?
[04:04] Jordan: yes, we maintain a model catalog with performance profiles. for lower latency we suggest smaller quantized variants or distillation models and pair with caching; for highest quality you can pick larger models and use caching/kv to manage costs. we can map this to your prompt patterns.
[04:22] [00:05:00] Priya: any compliance concerns if we move to Dedicated hosted by redwood vs Private on-prem? we have a mix of EU customers so data residency matters.
[04:33] Avery: Dedicated can be provisioned in region-specific clusters; we can ensure data stores remain in eu-west-1 if required. Private on-prem lets you keep everything behind your VPC.
[04:43] Maya: good to know. we want a phased approach: start with dedicated to reduce cost and then evaluate private if residency becomes blocking.
[04:51] Sam: sounds reasonable. we'll propose a 6-8 week pilot on Dedicated with a defined SLO and a rollback plan.
[04:59] Derek: on the pilot, can you do a simulated peak run at our expected 2x traffic? we want to see p95/p99 under load.
[05:08] Sam: yes — that's exactly what the bench will measure; we'll also capture token cost per 1k tokens at different batch windows.
[05:16] Maya: small aside — we saw a weird failure last week where the KV cache warmed up and then evicted unexpectedly, causing a latency spike. logs are attached in the ticket. any known issues?
[05:27] Jordan: there was a transient eviction bug tied to ttl estimation in older runtime versions; we rolled a fix two weeks ago. if your cluster hit that window maybe you saw it; can you share the trace and time?
[05:38] Maya: yes sent to support ticket #7894 — the spike lines up.
[05:43] Jordan: we'll correlate and confirm; apologies for that, and we'll prioritize if it's still happening.
[05:48] [00:07:00] Avery: ok security checklist: SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, and optional HSM for private. anything else on your side?
[05:58] Priya: we need support for customer-managed keys and a clear data retention policy.
[06:03] Avery: noted.
[06:05] Derek: one last product question — what's the timeline for the upcoming model upgrade you mentioned in the console notes? we saw a note about a v2 runtime and kernel improvements.
[06:15] Sam: that rollout is mid-march for the general pool; Dedicated pools can opt-in earlier for validation. the v2 runtime improves attention kernels for long sequences and yields better p99 in our internal tests.
[06:28] Maya: can we opt-in for a single node to test the v2 runtime?
[06:32] Sam: yes, that's part of the pilot scope. we'll coordinate.
[06:35] [00:10:00] Jordan: recap of agreed items so far: run dedicated pilot, bench p95/p99 under 2x traffic, send SOC2/KMS docs, and provide pricing bands.
[06:47] Maya: yep, and please include example config for prefix caching and a recommended quantization profile.
[06:53] Avery: absolutely — we'll include a recommended config and the expected cost delta.
[06:57] [00:12:00] Priya: on networking, we'll need VPC peering details and a diagram for firewall rules.
[07:04] Avery: we'll add a network diagram and sample terraform for the peering.
[07:09] Derek: thank you. any other blockers?
[07:13] Maya: timeline — we want to be in pilot within three weeks if possible.
[07:18] Sam: three weeks is tight but doable; we'll prioritize the bench and pricing.
[07:22] Jordan: i'll set calendar invites for the bench and a follow-up in two weeks.
[07:27] [00:15:00] Maya: one more note — we currently integrate embeddings for a retrieval layer; cost for embeddings also rose slightly. can you share suggestions for batching/embed caching strategies?
[07:37] Sam: yes, embeddings are a separate charge — caching and dedupe helps a lot; we can recommend a TTL and batching window to lower unit cost without hurting recency.
[07:47] Maya: perfect.
[07:49] Avery: OK we're at 30 minutes, i want to make sure we capture next steps: avery send usage, sam run bench, jordan share docs & invite, maya send traces. any additions?
[08:02] Priya: add network diagram + terraform.
[08:06] Avery: got it. final Qs?
[08:09] Derek: none. thanks all.
[08:11] Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the next 48 hours with the artifacts and schedule.
[08:14] [End at 15:45Z]
